setlist.title: Goin' Down The Road Feeling Bad

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Spanish Jam** (2 reviews): Reviewer always loves the Spanish Jam on this tape; Reviewer singles out the Spanish Jam as great [23][28]
- **Hell In A Bucket** (1 review): Bobby, sensing the crowd wasn't getting it, used some swear words during the song to rouse them [31]
- **Playin' In The Band** (1 review): Intense jamming runs from the start of Playin' to the start of Miracle; a friend called the space most intense ever [28]
- **Brokedown Palace** (1 other source): Listed as the encore [7]

## Setlist highlights

- **Three Mile Island rap**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [32]

## The recordings

- **gd1983-06-22.151456.unknown.miller.clugston.flac1648** (recommended): audience recording; 20 songs; 139 min [1]
- **gd1983-06-22.155966.fob.senn441.neumann.u87.blend.eaton.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 20 songs; 143 min [2]
- **gd1983-06-22.beyerm201.holbrook.burke.81511.sbeok.flac24**: source not stated; 20 songs; 140 min; rated 4.5/5 by 2 [5]
- **gd1983-06-22.136720.Unk-Hill.Keo.Flac1644**: audience recording; 21 songs; 140 min [7]. Said about its sound: Tape has some pauses between songs and a few missing pieces from tape flips [7]
- **gd83-06-22.senn-akg-mckeown.willy.14908.sbeok.shnf**: source not stated; 19 songs; 140 min; rated 3.67/5 by 21 [12]. Said about its sound: Audience recording so strong that Phil's bass rattles the listener's car mirror; State-of-the-art recording for its period, with punchy vocals and very little crowd noise; Full, rich audience recording with fine bass [20][21][22][23][24][27]

## Around the show

- First set is short and tight, and the pre-drums portion of the second set is very hot [20]
- Dosed, mooing crowd crossed the bridge off the island; the venue was dusty [25]
- Concertgoers crossed a grated metal walking bridge to the island, watching river waves beneath their feet [26]
- Left out of a Deadheads compendium II, so the show is obscure and easily overlooked [20]
- Reviewer found the first set better than the second [25]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1983-06-22.151456.unknown.miller.clugston.flac1648**: taped by Unknown; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Master Audience Cassettes (possibly 1st generation); Unknown equipment [1]. Also: Transfer by Charlie Miller, who also coordinated this combined effort; Chris Hecht's AKG d330bt and Sennheiser 421 blend source supplies a 7:27 patch in Drums > Space [1]
- **gd1983-06-22.155966.fob.senn441.neumann.u87.blend.eaton.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Rob Eaton; transferred by Rob Eaton, Scott Clugston; source: Rob Eaton's Master (FOB) Audience Cassettes; (2) Sennheiser 441's (Left + Right) + (1) Neumann U87 (center) blend > Nakamichi 550 [2]. Also: Recorded by Rob Eaton, who also handled the transfer and hard drive; Charlie Miller coordinated; FOB audience source supplies some crowd, the first notes of Deal, and a 0:49 patch in Drums [2]
- **gd1983-06-22.beyerm201.holbrook.burke.81511.sbeok.flac24**: taped by Kyle Holbrook; transferred by Tim Burke; source: Beyer M201 > Sony TC-D5M > TDK MA-R90 (No Dolby) [5]. Also: Tape flips occur after Ramble On Rose, after I Know You Rider, and during Spanish Jam [5]
- **gd1983-06-22.136720.Unk-Hill.Keo.Flac1644**: taped by Steve Hill; transferred by Keo; source: Master Audience Recorded By Steve Hill, Transfer By Keo; Unknown Mics > Unknown Number Of Decks Patched Out Of > Sony TC-D5M, Tapes: Maxell UDXLII C90's;… [7]
- **gd83-06-22.senn-akg-mckeown.willy.14908.sbeok.shnf**: source: 2 Sennheiser ME-80 and 2 AKG D-1000 mikes run through mixer>Sony D5M (30 feet from stage dead center. Recorded by Tommy McKeown)Note- This is the same source… [12]. Also: Taper Tommy lacked access to a PCM recorder, but the masters were well preserved; Reviewer owns a first-generation cassette that sounds amazing, possibly from the same setup; Reviewer taped with a Sony Walkman after everyone had trouble getting recorders onto the island; first-generation tape survives [21][28][31]
